shortened: To attain the pleasure of God is the most important thing. Thank God thou art content with the will of God and art attached in heart to His divine wishes; and as thou art thus, all thy desires will be granted thee.

order.why: Hear good pleasure described through the taste of love.
Explains contentment with divine decree through endurance of trials.
Read the desire for nearness.
shortened: O Javad! The heart's desire of every person of understanding is to increase in nearness to the Divine Threshold, and the wish of every wise one is to attain the good-pleasure of the Most Glorious Beauty, may my spirit be a sacrifice for His loved ones.

order.why: Consider acceptance as an exalted station.
shortened: The attainment of the good pleasure of God is the greatest of all stations. Until one drinks from this clear fountain that gives life to those nigh unto Him, one cannot ascend to the heights divine reunion or proximity.

order.why: Hear the value attributed to a single word of favor.
Keep the language of incomparable favor in its devotional setting.
shortened: His favor is better than a hundred thousand children, and His good-pleasure sweeter than a hundred thousand worlds. If thou attain this station and achieve this blessing, thou art possessed of the Kingdom. This is the most great bounty and the supreme bestowal.

order.why: Read the invitation to freedom from other claims.
shortened: Hearken unto the counsel of the Faithful Counselor and strive that thou mayest attain unto the most great gift, which is the good-pleasure of the One Friend, and become free and independent of all else.

order.why: Consider approval beyond public recognition.
shortened: To be approved of God alone should be one's aim.

order.why: Keep the reported warning about pleasing people in conversation with the opening.
shortened: All the people are negligent, they are not thinking of pleasing God and spreading the word of God. Notwithstanding it has been tried (and found out) that whoever tried to please the people displeased God, and he who tried to please God, became assisted and confirmed.

order.why: Read fame against the measure of acceptance.
Hear the reported prayer for a worthy life.
shortened: Pray that we may so live as to win the good-pleasure of the Blessed Perfection. Then all the doors will be opened before our faces.

order.why: Let the Bab’s prayer express the longing for acceptance.
shortened: All that I beg of Thee, O my God, is to enable me, ere my soul departeth from my body, to attain Thy good-pleasure, even were it granted to me for a moment tinier than the infinitesimal fraction of a mustard seed. For if it departeth while Thou art pleased with me, then I shall be free from every concern or anxiety; but if it abandoneth me while Thou art displeased with me, then, even had I wrought every good deed, none would be of any avail, and had I earned every honor and glory, none would serve to exalt me.

order.why: Read true understanding and the Crimson Ark.
Consider everlasting life as turning toward God.
shortened: Spirituality was my comfort, and turning to God was my greatest joy. If this had not been so, do you think it possible that I could have lived through those forty years in prison?
Thus, spirituality is the greatest of God's gifts, and 'Life Everlasting' means 'Turning to God'.

order.why: Introduce paradise through divine good pleasure.
Read the extended account of paradise here and beyond.
shortened: I swear by the Sun of the horizon of inner meanings that God has and will have paradises beyond compare. But in this first life, what is meant by paradise is His good-pleasure and entry into His Cause. And after the believers ascend from this world, they enter incomparable paradises and partake of boundless blessings, which are the fruits of their deeds in this world.

order.why: Keep its images from exhausting the realities they indicate.
shortened: Yes, in the divine utterances it is mentioned that paradise is the recognition of God and hellfire is separation from the Lord of Lords. The intent of this utterance is not that there is no divine realm or infinite bounty beyond this - God forbid! Rather, the meaning is that recognition and separation are like the tree, while bliss and torment in all divine worlds are like the fruit.
But in God's realm, for accepted souls there exists that which no eye hath seen, nor ear heard, nor hath entered into the heart of man.

order.why: Close the linked readings with humility before divine will.
shortened: Say: O people! Let not this life and its deceits deceive you, for the world and all that is therein is held firmly in the grasp of His Will. He bestoweth His favor on whom He willeth, and from whom He willeth He taketh it away. He doth whatsoever He chooseth.

order.why: Retain the supplied account of faith, deeds, and mercy.
Read the supplied Christian statement about grace.
End with the supplied account of effort and divine purification.

questions: How does the opening statement about being pleased with God’s servants change the way you understand divine good pleasure?
What distinguishes a deed offered sincerely from one treated as a way of securing a desired reward?
How do the passages hold human effort, obedience, and the free gift of grace together?
What does reading Ephesians through verse 10 add to its familiar statement about grace and works?
How can the warning against seeking public approval be read alongside the call to a generous relationship with others?
What possibilities open when paradise is understood through nearness and acceptance while its further realities remain beyond present comprehension?

references.label: 1 · Ephesians 2:8–10 · Gift and good works
references.note: The King James Version describes salvation through faith as God’s gift and excludes boasting in works; the next verse describes a life created in Christ for good works. Read the three verses together beside the compilation’s relationship between grace, effort, and conduct. This extends the supplied excerpt from Ephesians while leaving the distinct Christian and Baha’i theological settings visible.

subjects.displayTitle: Idolatry: when an image takes the place of truth
subjects.introduction: Whatever keeps a person from God is an idol, Bahá’u’lláh declares, even were it the highest thing in existence; and the idols, He adds, are vain desires and idle fancies. A deity assembled in a finite mind, a name clung to in place of the living authority it once pointed to, flattering words fashioned by one’s own hands and then bowed before, a self that becomes its own object of devotion: each is an image taking the place of truth, and ‘Abdu’l-Bahá’s distinction between a photograph kept for remembrance and one given extraordinary homage shows how fine the line can be. Most unsettling is the servant who worships idols while imagining he believes in God. The tale of Abraham’s rebuke of an idolatrous guest, and the divine patience that corrected him, pairs naturally with the Qur’án’s prohibition on reviling what others worship [1]. The journey leads on into the oneness of God, the temptations of anthropomorphism, the subtle lure of pantheism, and the heedlessness that lets any image quietly become a god.
subjects.arc: Begin with inward obstacles and the use of symbols, examine the critique of names and imagined authority, and return to recognition through humility.

order.why: Open with the expansive definition of an idol.
shortened: Say: Today, whatsoever preventeth you from God is an idol, even were it to be of the highest existence. For the excellence of every possessor of excellence lieth in his acknowledgment of God, his recognition of His Self, his entry beneath His shadow, and his prostration before His exalted and mighty Countenance.

order.why: Make the inward meaning of idols explicit.
Hear the related identification with vain desire.
Examine an idol fashioned from flattering words.
Turn the critique toward attachment to one’s own name.
shortened: By God! They worship names and perceive it not. Nay, were ye to ponder upon them, ye would find them to be worshippers of their own names.

order.why: Consider the idol of the self.
shortened: Say: O people, open your eyes! This is your Lord, the Chosen One, Who calleth you from the most exalted station with a wondrous tongue saying: Abandon the people and what they possess. They have clung to the idols of their own selves and are not among those who perceive.

order.why: Question an imagined deity within a finite mind.
Read the related account of imagination and objects.
shortened: One worships illusion, another imagines a god in his limited mind and worships that, when whatever fits in the mind is merely imagined. One worships the sun, another worships trees and stones. In ancient times many worshipped wind, worshipped the sea, worshipped plants.

order.why: Retain the reported broad claim in its own voice.
Distinguish remembrance from extraordinary homage.
Consider the conditional warning about personal attachment.
Read the brief episode with its source’s lesson in hospitality.
shortened: It is related that an aged and decrepit man became the guest of His holiness Abraham. He exercised toward his guest the utmost hospitality and courtesy. When dinner was served, his holiness Abraham uttered the Name of God and then started eating. On the other hand the guest uttered the name of an Idol and began to eat. His holiness was grieved, arose in wrath and rebuked his guest most severely.
But even, as he did so, God's revelation descended upon him:- "O Abraham! For a hundred years this man has been an idol worshipper and I have been patient with him.

order.why: Make room for the possibility of self-deception.
shortened: How many a servant hath worshipped idols while imagining he believed in God, Lord of all mankind.

order.why: Hear the warning addressed to those who feel guided.
Read the contrast between intention and actual allegiance.
shortened: The smoke of vain imaginings hath enveloped the world, and the veils of idle fancies have prevented the people from beholding the lights of the supreme horizon. They worship idols, supposing themselves to be worshipping the Truth.

order.why: Consider confidence that conceals a mistaken attachment.
Distinguish speech about God from the heart’s orientation.
shortened: They make mention of God with their tongues while their hearts tell of images and idols.

order.why: Examine names that conceal refusal of living authority.
shortened: It is as though they worship names for which God hath given no authority, and thus do they cleave to idols within themselves while perceiving not. They mention God without His authority being manifest to them, yet when it is manifested they turn back on their heels.

order.why: Read the related warning about worshipping names.
Consider names treated as independent lords.
Read the contrast between constructed temples and recognition.
shortened: Say: Have ye turned to temples made by the hands of Our servants while setting aside the Temple of God? This is naught but manifest wrong. Do ye imagine ye worship God your Lord? Nay, rather your vain imaginings, were ye of the perceiving ones.

order.why: Examine the use of inherited books to justify attachment.
shortened: Know thou that those who have taken idols as their guardians instead of God adduce as proof that these are the manifestations of the Cause among us, and when asked by what evidence they speak thus, they say: "We have found this in our books, therefore we follow them," and they are among those who have strayed from the path and then transgressed.
On that Day thou shalt find most of those on earth worshipping idols and rejoicing therein.

order.why: Hear the call to break vain imitation.
Keep the historical address to Persia in its setting.
Read the sequence of scriptural images of misplaced allegiance.
Consider the calf image and the Creator.
shortened: Do ye worship the calf and forsake Him Who created you by His command, by Whose light all who are in the heavens and earth are illumined, if ye be possessed of insight?

order.why: Hear the related warning about misidentification.
shortened: They drink fetid water while imagining it to be the water of life. They worship the calf while deluding themselves that it is the Lord of creation.

order.why: Question assurance of belonging while missing recognition.
shortened: Do ye worship the calf and forsake God, your Lord, and imagine that ye are numbered among the dwellers of the Paradise of refuge?

order.why: Read the appeal to turn toward nearness.
shortened: Follow not those who worship the calf instead of God - these are indeed far removed from the Tree of Nearness.

order.why: Keep the polemical and numerical claims attributed to their source.
Retain the reported historical narrative about Jeroboam.
Read the reported explanation of sun worship.
Consider the critique of elevating a lifeless form.
shortened: One retrogrades to such a low level as to worship statues and stony forms which are devoid of spirit and reason, while God hath conferred upon him reason and adorned his shoulder with the mantle of spiritual attributes!

order.why: Keep the reported claim about Hindu images in its historical voice.
Read the critique concerning images of Buddha as an attributed claim.
shortened: The attributes of Divinity are assigned to the idols of India and today the likeness of Buddha is worshipped by several hundred millions of human souls. What benefit does he draw from this adoration? Nothing.

order.why: Keep the reported account of church practices distinct.
Consider the contrast of a familiar summons with a new call.
shortened: They regard the sound of copper and brass as the divine call, though it be but inanimate matter, and they hold it sacred and answer its summons, rushing forthwith to church. But they deprive their ears of the divine call and show the utmost aversion to hearing the Word of Truth.

order.why: Read the warning against repeatedly creating new objects of allegiance.
Warns that worship can become idolatry through failure to recognize a new Revelation.
Turn toward understanding within revealed verses.
shortened: God willing, they will drink from the hidden oceans within the revealed verses and hold fast unto the peerless Friend, unlike the former people who each day took a different god, carved an idol, and worshipped it.

order.why: Hear the broad warning about private imaginings.
shortened: Every soul hath taken unto himself an idol besides God. Thus have vain imaginings and idle fancies seduced them.

order.why: Consider following desire as a form of turning away.
shortened: And among the people are those who follow their idle fancies and turn away from God, and are like unto them who worship idols and are devoted to them.

order.why: Read the contrast between an utterance and its reception.
shortened: The seas have been set ablaze by the fire of the word of the Chosen One, yet the people, having followed every ignorant idol, remain heedless thereof.

order.why: Hear the lament over misplaced allegiance.
Retain the concise statement of that contrast.
Keep judgment attributed to the text’s divine perspective.
Read the severe polemical language within its source setting.
shortened: They are as nothing, heedless ones, asses, fools. Were they to know, they would surely cut themselves to pieces and sacrifice themselves, their souls, their spirits, but they perceive not and worship what they know not, and they have taken for themselves a partner with God, the One, the Single, the Alone, the Mighty, the Beloved.

order.why: Retain the warning about leading others toward an idol.
shortened: And he who calleth the people unto the idol verily is to be numbered among the denizens of the coffin, and is thus recorded before the Throne.

order.why: Consider passion behind the choice of a helper.
Ask what the stated goal of allegiance reveals.
shortened: Say: Where is your goal, O company of vain imaginings? By God! If ye seek other than Me, it is but an idol unto you, did ye but know.

order.why: Read the invitation to open one’s eyes.
shortened: Fear ye nothing - open your eyes and follow not those who have taken their vain imaginings for their god and who cleave fast unto them.

order.why: Hear the warning against following imagined authority.
shortened: Say: Fear God, O peoples of the earth, and follow not those who have clung to the idols of fancy and vain imaginings.

order.why: Keep the counsel to leave opponents within its context.
Retain the related instruction about separation.
shortened: Shatter the idols of vain imaginings by the command of your Lord, the Mighty, the All-Knowing. Then cut yourself off from every sinful misbeliever.

order.why: Turn from attachment toward relinquishment.
shortened: Say: How long will ye sport with your idle fancies? How long will ye cleave to your idols? Cast away vain imaginings.

order.why: Hear the summons to release vain imaginings.
Read the concise call through the name of God.
Connect freedom from veils with recognition.
Consider remembrance that reorders other remembrances.
shortened: O Muhammad-Qasim! Shatter the idols of vain imaginings through the name of thy Lord, the Master of all beings, and remind the people through this Remembrance, before which all remembrances bow down when it appeareth.

order.why: Turn toward the dawning place of the signs.
shortened: Break the idols by My sovereignty and turn to the Dawning-Place of My signs - this is better for you, did ye but know.

order.why: Hear the appeal to divine power.
shortened: Say: Shatter the idols by the name of your Lord, the Mighty, the All-Knowing. Beware lest allusions hold you back; cast them behind you and hold fast unto this Cord whereby the worlds have been moved.

order.why: Read the related summons to break idols.
shortened: Beware lest you take the Evil One as your lord instead of God. Break the idols by the power of your Lord, the Master of all necks.

order.why: Approach the Abraham imagery through inward obstacles.
Consider the Abraham of faith as an image of liberation.
Join detachment with flight in divine love.
shortened: God willing, with the power of Abraham mayest thou shatter the idols of vain imaginings that have caused men to be veiled from the Dawning-Place of the Light of Divine Unity, and mayest thou soar in the atmosphere of the love of the All-Merciful on the wings of detachment.

order.why: Keep the historically gendered address and Abraham image visible.
shortened: Though thou art a woman, arise like unto a man and break the deity of idle imagination with the might of Abraham; render asunder the intervening veils with the power of the All-Glorious One; receive the Kawthar of meaning from the hand of the divine Youth and quaff it, and close thine eye to the whole world, for sight is created to behold the beauty of the Beloved, and heart has been brought into being for His recognition.

order.why: Read the praise of desires overcome.
Consider hearts turning after obstacles are removed.
Hear the affirmation addressed to women who recognize oneness.
shortened: The glory be upon you, O My handmaidens, and upon every handmaiden who hath broken the idols in the name of her Lord, the Possessor of all names, and hath acknowledged that which God acknowledged before the creation of the heavens and earth: that there is none other God but Him, the Powerful, the All-Knowing, the All-Wise.

order.why: Read gratitude for one who found a helper in God.
Consider the contrast of refusal and reception.
Let release from imaginings lead toward gladness.
Join certitude with joy and fragrance.
End with the Bab’s profession of allegiance to God.

questions: How does the definition of an idol as whatever obstructs recognition change the scope of the subject?
What distinguishes a symbol that supports remembrance from one that becomes an object of ultimate allegiance?
How might names, inherited ideas, or praise of oneself become resistant to fresh understanding?
What does the full story of Abraham’s guest add to the brief excerpt, especially when read beside Qur’an 6:108?
How can readers examine the compilation’s historical polemics while listening carefully to the beliefs and practices of people today?
What forms of humility could help someone test whether a cherished conviction brings greater recognition or conceals an unexamined attachment?

references.label: 1 · Qur’an 6:108 · Restraint in religious disagreement
references.note: Pickthall’s translation forbids reviling those invoked besides God, warning that this can provoke ignorant reviling in return. The verse also turns attention to how communities regard their own deeds and to their eventual return to God. Read this beside the inward critique of idols and the complete source of the Abraham episode, considering how theological disagreement and restraint in one’s treatment of others can coexist.
